status: REGISTERED 2026-11-17 before any recorded run; after a full-collection BMP correctness check (all 500 queries equal to the CPU reference) and smoke tests dev-bmp-01/02 (stopped by harness fixes: reuse-source rule, resource waits) and dev-bmp-03 (the design registered here). One development latency was seen (see development_disclosure)
recording: self-contained runtime gate (code/gate.py, a copy of experiments/2026-11-18-range-pruning/code/gate.py at 0dc7b3b, amendments 1 and 3) and self-recorded manifests; not recorded by the team runtime
question: How does BMP, the exact state-of-the-art CPU method, compare with the exact GPU scorers (range v2 and seeded range-bound pruning) on the same host (cuda5), index, queries and answers, at full scale?
hypothesis: None about the size of the gap. Published single-thread BMP reports 10.5 ms mean for this collection at k=10 on other hardware; our GPU scorers measured 0.49-0.72 ms mean on cuda5. This run replaces that cross-paper indication with a same-host measurement
contract: GSP-CAP32-U32GUARDED-NUMERIC-TIES-v1 for the GPU scorers and GSP-CAP32-U64-NUMERIC-TIES-v1 for BMP (uint64 sums); identical answers under the uint32 guard. All passages eligible, ties by original numeric passage ID, cap32 query weights

inputs.rule: checked by whole-file SHA-256 before any scoring, in this order
inputs.bmp_index_provenance: Built with the patched BMP ciff2bmp --bsize 32 (raw block bounds) from the pinned raw CIFF (SHA-256 16b111a409c557b966322c3b093e96a83c54a76e7863a0af4db3d0ae57043953, re-downloaded on cuda2 from the pinned Hugging Face revision and accepted on hash equality) on cuda2, a CIMS host with 251 GB RAM: the build peaked at 44.1 GB (22 min), which cuda5 could not spare; an attempt there pushed other users into swap and was stopped. The 13,448,678,853-byte output was streamed to cuda5; its SHA-256 eaf549b8... was computed on the stream and on the cuda5 file and is equal. No compressed-bound index was built (see implementations.bmp-b32)
inputs.pisa_queries_provenance: code/export_queries.py from the pinned GSP vocabulary; its first 25 lines are byte-identical to the 25-query file of the validated 1M BMP experiment (2026-11-11-bmp-resident-timing)
inputs.gpu_timing: the 9 timing CSVs and receipts of v2-w1024, prune-w1024-s64 and prune-w256-s64 in 20261117-cuda5-prune-04/raw, hashed by run.sh and checked against that run's manifest

fixed.host: cuda5 (2 x Xeon E5-2650 v2; BMP pinned to CPU 0, memory node 0)

implementations.bmp-b32: pisa-engine/BMP 67ad8c683fbc0c30145d1ee42c1dffbed8b12332 with the reviewed canonical patch (experiments/2026-11-10-bmp-correctness-fixes) and resident-context overlay (experiments/2026-11-11-bmp-resident-timing), timed by code/project_benchmark_single.rs: the validated project_benchmark adapter with its timed query() and monitor() functions byte-identical and only the second (compressed) index and the raw/compressed interleaving removed, so one 13.4 GB index is resident instead of two (about 24 GB, which risked pushing other users into swap on cuda5). Raw block bounds: the faster layout in the team's 1M timing (compressed 12.11% slower), so the stronger BMP baseline. Pinned Cargo.lock, cargo build --release --locked with cuda5's system Rust. Block size 32, alpha = beta = 1 (exact), one Rayon thread pinned to CPU 0, memory bound to node 0, queries in file order
implementations.gpu_compared: v2-w1024, prune-w1024-s64, prune-w256-s64 as recorded in range-pruning run 20261117-cuda5-prune-04 (binaries built and verified by 20261117-cuda5-prune-03)

timing_boundary: BMP: per query, from the resident index and the query text to the ordered TREC top-k string (cursor creation, query preparation, bounds, scheduling, scoring, top-k), the validated adapter's boundary. GPU: from the parsed (term, weight) pairs to the ordered top-k in host memory, including launches, synchronisation and result transfer. BMP's boundary additionally includes query-text parsing and TREC string construction, which favours the GPU slightly; this is stated wherever the comparison is reported

timing.order: BMP processes in sequence (the GPU side was timed in rotating order in its own run)
timing.before_each_process: wait (30 s polls, bounded by the deadline) until other users' CPU use over 5 s is at most CPU_LIMIT cores and at least 34 GiB of host memory is available. BMP holds about 26 GB resident (25.7 GB peak in development); the margin keeps it from being paged out or pushing other users into swap
timing.sampling: every 0.5 s: machine CPU time from /proc minus BMP and the sampler; the adapter records BMP's CPU jiffies (including iowait) and frequency before and after every round
timing.eligibility: a BMP timing process is ineligible if other users' CPU use averaged more than CPU_LIMIT cores, or if its CPU spent more than 1% of the measured rounds' time in iowait (the index was not resident, so the timing would measure the disk, not BMP); any other failure stops the run
timing.iowait_rationale: In a development check, one cold round on all 500 queries spent 321 s of its CPU time in iowait and 22 s computing (the 13.4 GB index is paged in lazily, on a machine that was swapping). The rule rejects any process whose timing includes paging
timing.replacement: ineligible processes are kept under raw/ineligible/ and replaced without a count limit; the run stops at a 12-hour wall-clock deadline and can be resumed from the same commit
timing.cpu_limit_rationale: the value of the range-pruning experiment, whose GPU timing is compared

correctness_gate: BMP's unit tests; a deliberate runtime-gate rejection (BMP CPU); BMP once on all 500 queries equal to the CPU reference; every timing process's answers equal to the CPU reference. The GPU side's answers were checked against the same reference in every timing process of prune-04. Any mismatch stops the run

analysis.primary: bmp-b32 / GPU scorer for v2-w1024, prune-w1024-s64 and prune-w256-s64: geometric mean over (process, query) pairs of median_bmp / median_gpu, pairing BMP process i with prune-04 process i of each GPU configuration and the same query
analysis.secondary: descriptive median, mean, p95, p99 per configuration; BMP's CPU-0 busy share per process from its own /proc/stat snapshots
analysis.interval: crossed process/query bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261118, percentile 2.5/97.5; conditional on the two sessions and the calibration queries

limits: one host; BMP single-threaded (its published setting) on a 2013 server CPU; GPU a 2023 consumer card
the BMP and GPU timings come from two sessions on the same host; pairing is by query and process index
BMP's timing boundary includes query-text parsing and TREC output, the GPU's does not (favours the GPU slightly)
shared machine; calibration queries only; held-out untouched
BMP is the exact state of the art; approximate methods (e.g. Seismic) are not compared
design: BMP is timed in this run (CPU only). The GPU side is the recorded timing of range-pruning run 20261117-cuda5-prune-04: same host, same verified binaries, same 500 queries and timing boundary, another session (2026-11-17 00:46-01:30 UTC). GPU latencies were consistent across five sessions (control median 0.686-0.690 ms), and re-timing them would need a quiet GPU, which is the scarce resource. The pairing is by query and process index across the two sessions, and every report states it
development_disclosure: Before registration one development round was seen (BMP on CPU 2, cold index, swapping machine: median 397 ms, dominated by iowait). No setting was chosen from it; it led to the memory threshold and the iowait rule
